evidenceBoundary: Primary-source guidance and product documentation; no local pipeline implementation, benchmark, test, build, deployment or performance claim.

sources.title: What is Continuous Delivery?
sources.documentedEvidence: Continuous delivery means maintaining software that can be delivered safely, quickly and sustainably on demand.
sources.proposedAdaptation: Keep releasability distinct from publication timing.
sources.limitation: Does not prescribe this project's cadence or prove its performance.

sources.title: Patterns: The Deployment Pipeline
sources.documentedEvidence: Build packages once, deploy the tested packages, and separate technical deployment from feature release.
sources.proposedAdaptation: Freeze each complete candidate and promote its identified platform artifacts.
sources.limitation: Its every-commit unit-test pattern conflicts with the initiative's complete-delivery gate; do not import that testing schedule.

sources.title: Control the concurrency of workflows and jobs
sources.documentedEvidence: One run executes per concurrency group. Default pending capacity is one with replacement; queue:max allows up to 100. FIFO follows waiting time, not dispatch time. queue:max cannot combine with cancel-in-progress:true.
sources.proposedAdaptation: Use explicit release sequence and freshness checks instead of assuming CI order is release order.
sources.limitation: Documentation capability is not proof of availability or correct configuration in the local workflows.

sources.title: Resource group
sources.documentedEvidence: Resource groups serialize sensitive jobs while independent build jobs can overlap. Modes include unordered, oldest_first, newest_first and newest_ready_first; newest modes require idempotent jobs. Nested dependencies can deadlock.
sources.proposedAdaptation: Model resource-specific exclusion separately from build execution and release selection.
sources.limitation: A process mode is neither an immutable artifact store nor a complete stale-publication policy.

sources.title: Deployment safety
sources.documentedEvidence: An older deployment can overwrite a newer one. GitLab offers outdated-job protection; its age uses job start time rather than commit time.
sources.proposedAdaptation: Check candidate sequence under the publication lock; make rollback an explicit separate action.
sources.limitation: GitLab's age rule is not a suitable substitute for a project-owned release order.

sources.title: Work in process limits
sources.documentedEvidence: Visualize the whole value stream, set WIP limits from capacity and measure lead time and variability.
sources.proposedAdaptation: Include unverified candidates, queued builds, failures and publication debt in WIP.
sources.limitation: No optimal numeric WIP limit or local velocity improvement is established.

sources.title: Working in small batches
sources.documentedEvidence: Small batches shorten feedback loops and support learning; delivering independent valuable increments requires deliberate scope.
sources.proposedAdaptation: Define each delivery as a complete meaningful increment with explicit acceptance.
sources.limitation: Does not authorize partial-code testing or establish a two-hour target.

sources.title: Monthly releases
sources.documentedEvidence: GitLab separates frequent deployments from scheduled customer releases, using release candidates and a final included commit.
sources.proposedAdaptation: Adopt predictable eligibility windows and freeze release content.
sources.limitation: Its monthly deadlines and multi-environment process are not a template to copy; skipping empty windows is a local adaptation.

sources.title: DL.CD.7: Remove manual approvals to practice continuous deployment
sources.documentedEvidence: Continuous deployment automates production delivery without manual approval; AWS labels this an optional capability.
sources.proposedAdaptation: Retain the project's human publication authority while automating preparation.
sources.limitation: Does not require removing this project's approval gates.
